altPaidOutFormula: noninterest expense 3.119077 − D&A 0.097968 − stock comp 0.271845 + income taxes paid 1.641663 (USD billions)
notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (FY2025 Form 20-F). Judgement: bank rule, not the payments formula. Nu is a deposit-funded lender: its operating cash flow is dominated by growth in credit-card receivables and loans (−22.75bn) and deposits (+12.86bn), not by collecting revenue, which is the condition that makes the formula meaningless for banks. So paidOut is null (comparable: false) and altPaidOut = noninterest expense − D&A − SBC + income taxes paid. Noninterest expense = transactional expenses (366,183) + total operating (expenses) income (2,752,894, net of 130,090 other income), from the income statement; expected credit loss (4,204,876) is a provision and interest and other financial expenses (4,578,680) are interest, both excluded as at BofA. D&A, SBC and taxes paid come from the cash-flow statement. Interest paid in cash (92,292) is far below interest expense (4,578,680); the cash-flow statement does not explain the gap, so it is recorded as stated. No xbrl objects: companyfacts has no FY2025 facts for Nu. All figures US$ thousands. Reports in USD.
